title: Bollywood Just Had Its Biggest Six Months Ever. One Man Earned Nearly Half of It.
excerpt: ₹2,075 crore in the first half alone. Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar accounts for more than half the total. And the second half hasn't even started.
body:
The numbers are in, the receipts are counted, and Bollywood just posted its biggest first half ever.

**₹2,075 crore nett.** That's what Hindi cinema collected at the Indian box office between January and June 2026 — comfortably the highest half-yearly total in the industry's history. With holdovers like **Welcome to the Jungle**, **Main Vaapas Aaunga**, and **Cocktail 2** still adding to the pile, that figure is expected to sail past ₹2,200 crore before July is over. For context, the first half of 2025 stood at just under ₹1,800 crore. This isn't a marginal improvement. It's a leap.

And one man is responsible for nearly half of it.

## The Ranveer Singh Show

**Ranveer Singh** has always been the industry's most electrifying presence, but in 2026, he became its most bankable. **Dhurandhar: The Revenge**, directed by **Aditya Dhar**, didn't just open big — it detonated. The spy-action sequel earned ₹1,186 crore nett in India alone, making it the highest-grossing Hindi film of all time. Its worldwide haul crossed ₹1,850 crore. The film has since expanded to Japan, chasing the kind of global footprint that only **Dangal** has managed before.

> "Ranveer mein ek bahot khaas quality hai" — Rakesh Bedi

It's not hyperbole anymore. Ranveer didn't just deliver a hit. He delivered the hit — the one that redefined what a Hindi film can earn. With **Pralay**, his ₹300-crore zombie thriller, already in pre-production for a September shoot in Australia, the man isn't slowing down. He's accelerating.

## Two Hits, Two Comebacks, and a Whole Lot of Misses

Beyond Dhurandhar's gravitational pull, the first half produced a handful of genuine success stories. **Border 2** earned ₹362 crore, riding patriotic fervour and **Sunny Deol**'s resurgent star power. **Bhooth Bangla** crossed ₹199 crore, proving that horror-comedy remains Bollywood's most reliable genre — and that **Akshay Kumar** can still open a film.

Speaking of Akshay, this might quietly be his most important year. After a brutal stretch of flops that had the industry writing him off, the man delivered *twice* in six months. Bhooth Bangla was the warm-up. **Welcome to the Jungle** — currently at ₹89 crore and climbing — looks set to become his third HIT of the era. Nobody saw that coming. At 58, Akshay Kumar just reminded everyone that the only thing more dangerous than counting him out is betting against him.

**The Kerala Story 2: Goes Beyond** and **Mardaani 3** emerged as solid successes, both finding their audiences without the benefit of massive opening weekends. **Main Vaapas Aaunga**, Imtiaz Ali's poetic return with **Kartik Aaryan**, is still legging its way toward HIT territory.

But the misses were brutal. **Cocktail 2** opened well at ₹14 crore but collapsed within days — a textbook case of audience rejection after a promising trailer. **Pati Patni Aur Woh Do**, **Ikkis**, **O Romeo**, **Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai**, and **Ek Din** all underperformed, some catastrophically. The middle ground — that ₹50-to-150-crore zone where mid-budget films used to live comfortably — is becoming an endangered species. You either hit ₹200 crore or you don't hit at all.

## What It Means for NRIs

For diaspora audiences, the takeaway is simple: Bollywood is producing fewer films that demand your attention, but the ones that do are *spectacular*. Dhurandhar played to packed IMAX houses from New Jersey to London. Welcome to the Jungle is currently outpacing every Akshay Kumar overseas release since Sooryavanshi. The theatrical experience is worth it again — if you're picking the right films.

And the streamers are catching on. **Peddi** just landed on Netflix. **Ikka** arrives July 10. **Pritam and Pedro** is already on JioHotstar. The pipeline from theatre to living room has never been shorter, which means even films you missed on the big screen will find their way to you within weeks.

## The Second Half Could Be Even Bigger

If the first half belonged to Ranveer, the second half belongs to everyone. **Alpha** opens tomorrow with **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari** making history as the Spy Universe's first female leads. **Dhamaal 4** follows on July 10. **Christopher Nolan**'s **The Odyssey** arrives July 17 with a cast that reads like an Oscar ballot. **Awarapan 2** brings **Emraan Hashmi** back from the dead — literally — on Independence Day.

And then there are the titans waiting in the wings. **Drishyam 3** on Gandhi Jayanti. **Ramayana: Part One**, arguably the most anticipated Indian film in a generation, with **Ranbir Kapoor** as Lord Ram. **Shah Rukh Khan**'s **King**, closing out the year with what promises to be a father-daughter action spectacle.

₹2,075 crore in six months. The only question now is whether the second half can match it — or blow it away entirely.
